Authored by Dr. K. M. Nahid-Ul-Haque (MBBS MMC; Diploma in Endocrinology, BIRDEM),
Diabetes, Thyroid & Hormone Care, Faridpur — 27 August 2026, via the questionnaire in
His own framing, kept because it governs how these numbers may be used: 'These
percentages are synthetic-data priors, not epidemiological estimates. They have been
normalized for internal consistency and are not audited prevalence figures. No
patient-level data were used.' Nothing here is a source for a clinical claim.
Versioned so a dataset generated months from now is reproducible, and so that changing
the profile is a visible decision rather than a quiet drift in what 'realistic' means.
authoredBy: Dr. K. M. Nahid-Ul-Haque, DTHC Faridpur
recalibration: Permitted when prospective, consented, properly governed aggregate clinic data become available.

population.$comment_visits: 70% new / 30% follow-up on a clinic day is unusual for an established practice and is flagged for confirmation — it drives queue volume and the whole visit-generation model.

presentingProblem.$comment: Share of caseload by the MAIN problem attended for. Sums to 1.00.

diabetes.$comment: Type shares sum to 1.00 within the diabetes caseload.

atTargetAfterOneYear.$comment: Among those retained in care — not of all who present.

complicationAtFirstVisit.$comment: At least one established microvascular or macrovascular complication.

thyroid.$comment: Shares sum to 1.00 within the thyroid caseload.

tshHypothyroid.$comment: Occasional values above 100 — the tail is real and worth generating.

tshHyperthyroid.$comment: Lower bound is undetectable, not zero — the generator must be able to emit 'undetectable' rather than a number.

otherConditions.$comment: Overall share of the whole caseload, not of a subgroup.

pcos.notes: Reproductive-age women; irregular cycles, hyperandrogenic features, obesity/metabolic risk, subfertility commonly coexist.

osteoporosis.notes: More often postmenopausal women, or assessment for secondary causes.

maleSexualReproductive.notes: Erectile dysfunction, premature ejaculation, low libido, hypogonadism, infertility. Metabolic and thyroid comorbidity common.

comorbidity.$comment: Denominators differ per row and are stated. Treating these all as a share of the whole caseload would be wrong.

hypertension.denominator: adults with type 2 diabetes or metabolic disease

dyslipidaemia.denominator: adults with type 2 diabetes or metabolic disease

fattyLiver.denominator: type 2 diabetes, obesity or metabolic syndrome

prescribing.$comment: Shares overlap — combination therapy is the norm here, so these do not sum to 1.
prescribing.firstLineType2: Metformin 500 mg once or twice daily with food, titrated toward 1,500–2,000 mg/day. Early combination therapy is common because many present near HbA1c 10%; empagliflozin 10 mg od added when appropriate, linagliptin 5 mg od used selectively.
prescribing.commonTwoDrug: Empagliflozin 10 mg + linagliptin 5 mg od, commonly fixed-dose; metformin often continued separately.
prescribing.commonThreeDrug: Metformin 1,500–2,000 mg/day + empagliflozin 10 mg od + linagliptin 5 mg od.
prescribing.insulinRegimen: Basal insulin, usually glargine; human premixed 30/70 also common. In pregnancy, split-mixed human insulin, individualised.
prescribing.statin: Rosuvastatin 5–10 mg od or atorvastatin 10–20 mg od; intensity increased for ASCVD or high cardiovascular risk.
prescribing.localDeviation: No major systematic deviation. Follows ADA and other international guidance, adapted for affordability, medicine availability, renal function, pregnancy and patient preference.

namesAndLanguage.$comment_language: Not merely a test-data fact — a product finding. The record is mixed-script BY DEFAULT: Bangla prose, English clinical terms. This bears on CP29 onward and on the open question about Bengali numerals.

generatorRequirements.$comment: From the clinician's own free-text answer. Not all of this is buildable at CP13 — the checkpoint that can implement each is named.

preserveRelationships.requirement: Realistic relationships among age, sex, diagnosis, laboratory values, medicines and contraindications.

realisticMissingness.requirement: Retain realistic missingness, delayed tests, missed visits and loss to follow-up.
realisticMissingness.$comment: Frequently forgotten in synthetic data, and the omission makes every downstream screen look tidier than reality.

doseAdjustment.requirement: Dose changes driven by eGFR, pregnancy, hepatic status and hypoglycaemia risk.

careProcesses.requirement: Model care processes as well as diagnoses: diet/exercise/weight counselling, adherence and affordability, injection technique, sick-day and fasting and hypoglycaemia education, foot care, complication screening, pregnancy and preconception status, mental health, referrals, proactive team follow-up.
careProcesses.$comment: Each needs the table that records it. None of those tables exist yet.

testCases.$comment: Named by the clinician as the cases the software must be exercised against. The generator should be able to produce each on demand, not merely by chance.
